topics.topicName: Parts of a Sentence: Subject and Predicate
topics.chapterOrSection: Chapter 1: Parts of a Sentence (Sections A & B)
topics.teaches: Meaningful word order; Subject as who/what the sentence is about and Predicate as what is said about the Subject; single-word vs multi-word Subjects/Predicates; identifying the head-word (noun in Subject, verb in Predicate); split predicates in interrogatives ('Have you finished your work?'); understood 'you' in imperatives; omitted 'it/is' in exclamatory sentences.
examples: Ashok was a great king.
The boys in our school play football.
Stop! -> (You) Stop!
What a beautiful flower! -> (It is) a beautiful flower!
exerciseTypes: Marking head-words in multi-word Subjects and Predicates (Act. 4-7)

topics.topicName: Sentence, Subject and Predicate, Enlargement & Predicate Elements
topics.teaches: Sentence as ordered words making complete sense; Subject (उद्देश्य) and Predicate (विधेय); Finite verb defined as verb governed by Subject's Number and Person; understood 'you' in imperatives; 6 Kinds of Subject and 9 Subject Adjuncts; Predicate breakdown into Finite Verb, Transitive/Intransitive, Objects (Direct, Indirect, Cognate, Reflexive, Adverbial, Retained), and Complements.
examples: Birds fly.
The sun rises in the east.
Sit down. (Subject: you understood)
The old man living in that hut gave me a book.
exerciseTypes: Splitting sentences into Subject, Adjuncts, Verb, Object, and Complement

topics.topicName: Simple and Complex Sentences (Subject & Predicate mention)
topics.teaches: Briefly states 'A simple sentence has one subject and one predicate' on p. 53 with two underlined examples before moving directly to clause identification and sentence transformation.
examples: He went to market.
The train was late by two hours.

topics.topicName: Types of Sentences (Finite Verb, Simple Sentence Patterns, Compound & Complex)
topics.teaches: Assumes prior Subject/Predicate knowledge; defines finite verb and clause; classifies Simple sentences by function (Declarative, Interrogative, Imperative, Exclamatory) and structure patterns (SV, SVO, SVOO, SVC, SVOC); Compound and Complex sentences.
examples: The night is dark. (SVC)
They elected him president. (SVOC)

topics.teaches: Distinguishes Time (Past, Present, Future) from Tense; teaches that English verbs have ONLY TWO TENSES (Present and Past) and 'there is no future tense in English'; explains 3 verb forms (v, v-ed, -ed/-en), 8 Tense x Aspect combinations (Simple, Progressive, Perfect, Perfect Progressive in Present & Past), stative/non-progressive verbs (p. 43), for/since, used to/would, and ways to express Future Time (modals, be going to + v, Present Progressive, Present Simple, be about to, will be v-ing, will have v-en, be + to + infinitive).
examples: The sun rises in the east. (Present Simple - universal truth)
I am writing a letter now. (Present Progressive)
The train leaves at 5 p.m. tomorrow. (Present Simple for future time)
We are going to visit Puri next week. (Future time expression)
exerciseTypes: Fill in blanks with correct verb forms
Matching time reference to tense/aspect form
Correcting stative verbs misused in progressive form

topics.teaches: Reaffirms the 2-tense (Present & Past) + 3-time model from Class IX; consolidates Present Simple/Progressive for Present Time, 6 ways of expressing Past Time (Past Simple, Past Progressive, Present Perfect, Present Perfect Progressive, Past Perfect, Past Perfect Progressive), and 5 ways of expressing Future Time (will/shall, be going to, Present Progressive, Present Simple, be about to / will be v-ing / will have v-en).
examples: When we reached the station, the train had already left.
I have lived here for ten years.
It is going to rain.
exerciseTypes: Choosing between Past Simple and Present Perfect / Past Perfect

topics.topicName: Use of Tenses & Sequence of Tenses (12-Tense Model)
topics.teaches: Uses traditional 3-Tense x 4-Aspect = 12-Tense framework (Present, Past, Future x Indefinite, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous); summarises usage rules and signal adverbs, assuming basic conjugation is already known; teaches Sequence of Tenses between principal and subordinate clauses.
examples: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. (Present Indefinite)
She had finished her homework before I arrived. (Past Perfect)
He said that honesty is the best policy. (Sequence of Tenses exception)
exerciseTypes: Fill in the blanks with correct tense of bracketed verbs (Ex. 1 p. 102)

topics.topicName: Tense (Time vs Tense, 3 Tenses, 12 Sub-types, Conjugation & Errors)
topics.teaches: Distinguishes Time (समय) from Tense (काल) in L1, then explicitly teaches a 3-Tense model (Present, Past, Future) divided into 12 sub-tenses (dual labels: Indefinite/Simple, Continuous/Progressive, Perfect/Non-Progressive, Perfect Continuous/Perfect Progressive); details Strong, Weak, Invariant, and Mixed verbs; gives full person/number conjugation tables; lists stative non-continuous verbs, for/since, and 15 common errors.
examples: The earth moves round the sun.
I have been reading since morning.
Tomorrow is Sunday. / He leaves for Delhi tomorrow.
exerciseTypes: Fill in blanks with correct tense

topics.topicName: Introductory Subject-Verb Agreement (Basic, Count/Uncount, Pair & Quantifier Rules)
topics.teaches: Foundational person/number verb table ('I am, We/You/They are, He/She/Mina is, The teacher and the students are, The cow eats, Cows eat', p. 32) explicitly noting full SVA comes later; singular/plural agreement with countables vs uncountables (p. 83), pair nouns vs 'a pair of' (p. 85), collective & 'police/people/cattle' (p. 86), '-s' singular uncountables like Mathematics/Diabetes (pp. 88-89), quantifiers (p. 93), and 'The rich/blind' + plural verb (pp. 98-99).
examples: The teacher and the students are in the classroom.
My trousers are new. / A pair of trousers is on the bed.
The police have caught the thief.
Mathematics is an interesting subject.
exerciseTypes: Choosing correct verb forms in Activities (Ch. 7 Act. 4, Ch. 8)

topics.chapterOrSection: Chapter 3: Subject – Verb Agreement (and Ch. 4 p. 31 Finite Verb note)
topics.teaches: Core Number & Person rule plus 16 numbered rules: (1a) preparatory 'there', (1b) 'it', (2) plural sums/distances/weights as single unit, (3a) 'and' denoting single notion, (3b) 'and' compound plural, (4a) collective nouns unit vs individuals, (4b) police/people/poultry/cattle, (5) uncountables (clothing/food/furniture/scenery), (6) intervening phrases/clauses, (7a) either/neither/none of (+ informal plural note), (7b) each/one of, (7c) no/some, (7d) 'and' with one vs two determiners, (8) fractions/percentages, (9a) a lot of/some of, (9b) a crowd/herd/group of, (9c) a number of vs the number of, (10) -s nouns (Statistics/Physics/News/Measles), (11) clause subjects, (12a) with/as well as/together with, (12b) not only...but also/either...or/neither...nor nearer subject, (13) pair nouns vs 'a pair of', (14) The rich/blind, (15) plural titles/country names (Gulliver's Travels/United States), (16) relative pronoun antecedents. Note: Ch. 3 Act. 3(i) p. 30 tests tag 'I am young and strong, (amn't / aren't)?'.
examples: Ten kilometres is a long walk.
Bread and butter is a wholesome food.
The number of students in our class is forty.
Neither the teacher nor the students were present.

topics.topicName: Concord: Agreement of the Verb with Subject (13 Rules + Exceptions)
topics.teaches: 13 numbered concord rules + exceptions: Number/Person & head-noun matching; 'and' plural vs single idea/same person/'each & every'; 'or/either...or/neither...nor' (singular, plural last, nearest person); 'with'; 'not only...but also'; 'there'; 'either/neither/each/everyone/one of' strictly singular; plural-form singular nouns (Mathematics/Politics/wages/news/United States/Gulliver's Travels); collective nouns; relative pronoun antecedent; sums of money.
examples: The quality of these apples is good.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Each boy and each girl was given a prize.
He as well as his friends is responsible.
exerciseTypes: Selecting between verb options in sentences (Exercises 2-6, pp. 102-104)

topics.topicName: Scattered Subject-Verb Agreement Rules (No Standalone Chapter)
topics.teaches: No standalone SVA chapter; rules distributed across: Finite verb agreeing with Subject Number/Person (Ch. 1 p. 3); cattle/people/police vs mathematics/physics/news (Ch. 4 Ex. 4 pp. 50-51); distributive pronouns 'each/every/either...or/neither...nor/each of/neither of' strictly singular (Ch. 5 pp. 66-67, 73); 'The Secretary and Headmaster is' vs 'The Secretary and the Headmaster are' (Ch. 6 p. 80); 'Many a man' vs 'A great many men' (Ch. 6 p. 84); 'Bread and butter is/are' test item (Ch. 12 p. 201).
examples: The Secretary and Headmaster is coming.
The Secretary and the Headmaster are coming.
Many a man has done this.
Neither of the two boys was present.

topics.topicName: Non-MVP Grammar Topics Across the Four Textbooks
topics.teaches: Comprehensive Class 9-10 grammar outside the 3 MVP modules: Determiners & Articles; Auxiliaries & Modals (plus Assam 24 Anomalous Finites); Noun Phrases, Pre/Post-Modifiers, Countables & Uncountables; Adjectives & Comparison; Adverbs, Adverbials & Negative Inversion; Prepositions & Phrasal/Group Verbs; Non-Finites; Conjunctions; Simple, Compound & Complex Sentences; Noun, Relative & Adverb Clauses; Conditionals; Active & Passive Voice; Direct & Indirect (Reported) Speech; Negatives, Interrogatives, Question Tags & Transformation of Sentences; Clause Analysis; Punctuation.

class9.odishaClass9: Covers foundational grammar in 12 chapters: Parts of a Sentence (Word order, Subject & Predicate, Word Classes, 4 Sentence Types), Verbs (Main/Auxiliary + introductory SVA table), Time and Tense (2-Tense model + Future Time), Auxiliaries, Noun Phrase & Modifiers, Countables & Uncountables (incl. pair/collective/-s noun SVA), Determiners (quantifier SVA), Adjectives, Adverbs/Adverbials, Negatives/Interrogatives, and Predicate Phrase patterns.
class9.psebClass9: Covers 9 grammar chapters: Determiners, Modals, Prepositions, Conjunctions, Simple & Complex Sentences (brief 1-line Subject/Predicate mention), Voice, Narration, Non-Finites, and Tenses (12 traditional tenses + 13 Concord rules + Sequence of Tenses), followed by Composition (Vocabulary, Reading, Letters/E-mails, Paragraphs).
class9.assamCombined9_10: Single combined Classes IX & X textbook with no explicit Class 9 vs Class 10 chapter split.

class10.odishaClass10: Builds directly on Class 9 in 10 chapters: Tense Revisited (consolidating 2-tense + 3-time mastery), Types of Sentences (Finite verb/clauses, SV-SVOC patterns, Compound/Complex), dedicated Subject-Verb Agreement (16 formal rules), Non-Finite Verb Forms, Prepositions, Phrasal Verbs, Noun & Relative Clauses, Adverb Clauses & Conditionals, The Passive, and Direct & Indirect Speech.
class10.psebClass10: No Class 10 PSEB textbook was supplied among the uploaded sources (gap documented in content-gaps.md).
class10.assamCombined9_10: Shares all 17 grammar chapters and 6 vocabulary chapters across Classes 9 and 10 without grade-level differentiation.

verifiedConflictsAndNotes.description: Odisha Class IX (Ch. 3 pp. 33-34) and Class X (Ch. 1 p. 1) teach that English verbs have only 2 tenses (Present & Past) and no future tense; PSEB Class IX (Ch. 9 p. 94) and Assam IX-X (Ch. 9 pp. 121-126) teach 3 tenses and 12 sub-tenses (Present/Past/Future x 4 aspects).
verifiedConflictsAndNotes.handlingPolicy: Never silently merge. Document both models transparently and align Grammar Quest teaching notes by board/class expectation.

verifiedConflictsAndNotes.description: Odisha uses Simple/Progressive and v/v-ed/v-en/φ+v; PSEB uses Indefinite/Continuous and V1/V2/V3; Assam uses dual labels plus Strong/Weak/Mixed verbs, Anomalous Finites, and Non-conclusive verbs.
verifiedConflictsAndNotes.handlingPolicy: Expose equivalent terminology badges clearly without contradicting either board.

verifiedConflictsAndNotes.description: Odisha Class IX Ch. 11 p. 136 states "I'm not" (not "I amn't"), whereas Assam Ch. 3 p. 26 lists "amn't" and Odisha Class X Ch. 3 Act. 3(i) p. 30 tests "I am young and strong, (amn't / aren't)?".
verifiedConflictsAndNotes.handlingPolicy: Teach standard "aren't I?" in MVP practice/assessment and flag the internal Odisha IX vs X/Assam discrepancy in content-gaps.md.

verifiedConflictsAndNotes.description: Odisha Class X Ch. 3 Rule 7a (p. 26) notes informal conversational plural verbs after 'neither of / none of / either of', while PSEB Class IX (p. 99) and Assam (pp. 66-67, 73) require singular verbs strictly.
verifiedConflictsAndNotes.handlingPolicy: Teach formal singular agreement as the standard exam/MVP rule while explicitly noting Odisha Class X's informal usage caveat.

verifiedConflictsAndNotes.description: Odisha Class IX Ch. 12 (pp. 141, 144) labels locative adverbials like 'in the garage' in 'He kept the car in the garage' as Complement (C) in VG+O+C+(Adjunct), whereas Assam Ch. 1 & 13 classify location phrases as Adjuncts/Adverbials.
verifiedConflictsAndNotes.handlingPolicy: Keep Module 1 focused on Subject vs Predicate boundary and head-words rather than advanced Clause Element disputes.
